items.label: INNIO Q2 FY2026 (07-28-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Large orders (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: the Q2 highlight was a 1.

set.signal: Large orders (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: the Q2 highlight was a 1.1 GW order from a megascale data center customer (not named), one of the largest orders in INNIO's history, with more than 200 Jenbacher J624 engines expected to provide behind-the-meter prime power and delivery until 2031. Martin Widner: the order is 'even below 30%' of the quarter's data center order intake; part of it is containerized (more scope) and part is for a powerhouse installation (less scope). CFO Dennis Schulze: 'Size of 1.1 GW is not the exception, it's now, I would say, common.' CEO: 'we announced the Greco [as transcribed; INNIO's same-day Q2 results release, INNIO 8-K (07-28-2026), names the counterparty of its multi-year ~1.25 GW gas-engine framework agreement as Rehlko] one was 1.25 GW. It's a little bit longer run project'; 'we are working with Greco, a long-term contract delivering engines Type four, Type six. There are many of these coming up.'

items.reason: The defeatbeta transcript renders the customer of the 1.25 GW long-term engine contract as 'Greco'; INNIO's own release of the same day names the ~1.25 GW multi-year framework agreement's counterparty as Rehlko. The verbatim word stays, the release's name is added in the bracket (no inference: same company document, same 1.25 GW).
items.evidence: 8-K EX-99.1: 'Multi-year strategic framework agreement with Rehlko, securing supply of approximately 1.25 GW of gas engine capacity over three years' | call: 'we announced the Greco one was 1.25 GW'
